messages:
Incident Bot: [PAGER] dedicated-router degraded: spike in router fallback events for us-east-1 -> us-west-2. Auto-fallback policy triggered repeatedly. Affected: dedicated-prod-us-east pool. Pager sent to @eng-oncall @eng-sre. Incident INC-3471 created.

Alex K: seeing this, joining now. what are the exact symptoms?

Priya S: alerts show router fallback count jumped at 23:01 UTC, then autoscaler started draining nodes in dedicated-prod-us-east at 23:03. Looks like router rerouted traffic to a variant that isn't accepting connections -> subsequent capacity signals show 0 free_slots.

Sam T: graphs: http://grafana.redwood/board/routers?from=23:00 to=23:10 - router_fallbacks + pool_drains. Also seeing capacity_proxy:free_slots metric oscillating between 0 and 128 every ~30s.

Maria G: that oscillation smells like a stale heartbeat / proxy reporting ghost capacity. Could be proxy-heartbeat-lag after recent proxy roll. Anyone rolled the capacity-proxy?

Jamal R: I rolled capacity-proxy in us-east an hour ago for the retry fix. Deploy bot said success. Not seeing obvious errors in the deploy logs.

Alex K: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable auto-fallback policy for dedicated-prod-us-east (so router doesn't keep switching variants) 2) temporarily pin routing to primary variant for high-risk customers 3) block autoscaler from draining until we confirm capacity signals are correct.

ops-rotation: acknowledged, applying mitigation 1 -> disabling fallback for us-east now.

Sam T: disable command: ``redwoodctl routing set-fallback-policy --region us-east-1 --policy disabled``

ops-rotation: done. router config shows fallback_policy=disabled for us-east. :white_check_mark:

Priya S: pinned routing: ``redwoodctl route pin --pool dedicated-prod-us-east --variant primary-v2 --duration 30m`` (pin applied).

Maria G: blocking autoscaler drain: ``kubectl patch hpa dedicated-prod-us-east --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4,"maxReplicas":20}}'`` bumped min to avoid immediate drains.

Jamal R: good. I'm pulling capacity-proxy logs from the node that reports ghost values. tail: ``/var/log/capacity-proxy.log`` shows repeated "heartbeat delayed by 45s" errors around 23:02. Paste: ```2026-02-18T23:02:05Z WARN heartbeat: last heartbeat 45s ago, computed_free_slots=128; 2026-02-18T23:02:36Z ERROR grpc: connection reset by peer```

Alex K: that matches. Router sees ephemeral 0 free_slots when the proxy misses heartbeat -> router interprets as capacity exhausted and triggers fallback to alternate variant. Fallback then stresses other pools which can cause autoscaler reactions and create loop.

Priya S: customer impact: looks like 12 active customers had degraded latency or 5xx increases. Top affected: acme-inc (SL high-priority), note: partial errors only for dedicated-backed routes.

Sam T: quick query to find impacted keys: ``select count(*) from requests where region='us-east-1' and status>=500 and timestamp>='2026-02-18T23:00'`` returns 274 errors across 12 customers.

Maria G: recommended next steps: - keep fallback disabled until proxy heartbeat issue fixed - restart capacity-proxy on suspected nodes - run a one-off reconciliation job to reconcile free_slots with actual container count - add a short debounce window in router to ignore single-missed heartbeats (prevents immediate fallback).

Jamal R: restarting proxy on node ip 10.12.8.45 now. Will tail logs and report.

ops-rotation: restarted. New logs show steady heartbeats: ```2026-02-18T23:05:12Z INFO heartbeat: OK interval=5s computed_free_slots=32```

Sam T: after restart, router_fallbacks dropped from ~450/min to ~3/min over 2 minutes. Autoscaler stopped initiating drains.

Alex K: great. I'll escalate to eng-infra to get a postmortem on the capacity-proxy deploy that may have caused heartbeat lag. Also, we need an ops action to add a guard in the router: treat a single missed heartbeat as jitter, require 2 consecutive misses within 20s before triggering fallback.

Priya S: filing a follow-up ticket: INFRA-1127 (capacity-proxy heartbeat resilience + router debounce). I'll add notes about the customer list and the recommended config changes.

Maria G: customer communication: recommend a short note to acme-inc and others: "We experienced transient routing failures in us-east-1 between 23:00-23:06 UTC which resulted in increased errors for dedicated deployments. We disabled an automatic fallback policy and restarted a proxy to restore steady capacity signals. No data loss; root cause under investigation."

Alex K: agreed. @ops-rotation please keep fallback disabled for 30 minutes, monitor graphs, and if stable, re-enable with safe debounce config.

ops-rotation: will monitor. current status: fallback disabled, pinned primary variant, proxy restarted, autoscaler min bumped.

Jamal R: will follow up with logs and k8s event dump to the incident: http://incidents.redwood/INC-3471.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-3471 updated: severity=sev2, status=mitigated, responders=[Alex K, Priya S, Sam T, Maria G, Jamal R].

Alex K: handing off to next oncall in 20m. If anything flares, wake me. otherwise I'll write the initial postmortem tomorrow.

Priya S: thanks team. I'll draft customer comms and the infra ticket.

Sam T: quick note for follow-up: consider a canary for capacity-proxy rollouts that exercises heartbeat under load. we shouldn't rely on a single deploy path.

Maria G: agree. Also add an automated test to the router that simulates a delayed heartbeat and ensures debounce logic prevents immediate fallback.

ops-rotation: monitoring looks green at 23:09 UTC. closing pager for now, will reopen if metrics cross thresholds. :thumbsup:

Alex K: thanks all.
